chapter: Leading the band after Chick Webb, 1939-40
title: "Goodnight My Love" and Ella on Goodman's Camel show
summary: Jack Robbins gave the band the hit first; Ella sight-read arrangements quickly, and Goodman borrowed her and the arrangement for his broadcast.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: Robbins used to give us all these big hit songs, and we'd have them before any band would have them?
Well, this one particular song we had -- the name of the song was "Goodnight My Love." That was the song (inaudible). You asked me on the interview what was the song that Ella did.
The song was so popular and Benny Goodman asked could he use Ella in his arrangement for (inaudible) broadcast of this number (inaudible), because it was number one.
We had it before anybody had it. We played -- Jack Robbins used to give us all these hit songs. (Inaudible) copies and (inaudible) record it.
I tell you one thing, if anybody at that time -- if Ella --
Like, we used to pick all of her songs. A lot of publishers would come up and give us songs -- top publishers. Mills Music, Robbins, Shapiro-Bernstein, you name them -- all the top publishers.
Everybody was trying to get Ella to do the top hit songs.
Well Jack Robbins gave us this song,

"Goodnight My Love." And when Ella did this song, whoever had to come behind her, they was just like catching up.
Because Ella would do a -- we would rehearse an arrangement on a pop song. (Inaudible) He would be sittin' up with plain little cards (inaudible).

And Chick would say, "Okay, Ella, we're ready." She'd come over and we'll hand her the sheet. (Inaudible). She could sight read better than of all the singers fast anybody (inaudible). She was real (inaudible). We'd be (inaudible) rehearsing the arrangements, she be listening, you know. She say, "Okay, yall ready for me?" "Yeah."

I remember one afternoon we were rehearsing a song, "Goodnight My Love." It became a smash hit. We had it before (inaudible), because remember I told you we used to broadcast every Saturday afternoon from the Savoy Ballroom?
Yeah.
From 5:30 to 6. 6:30, or something like that. Anyway, when we did this number, it became very popular.
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
(Inaudible), "Can Ella do Goodnight Camel My Love?" So Benny had the Camel Show -- the Camel (Inaudible) Camel Show.
He wanted Ella to sing this song on his show, (inaudible) the girl-- I think Helen Forrest -- whoever he had singing with him at that time.
So Ella did the song with Benny Goodman and used our arrangement of it. It became a very big hit.
I don't know if he recorded that with her or not. I think he wanted her to record it.
But this was one of the big songs that we was doing at that time. This was just one of the pop songs that we had.
The band was really on its way. We were really on our way then -- with a double attraction, Ella and Chick Webb's band (Unintelligible).
The band was really on its way just before he passed away.
